title: Mitred square — striped
subtitle: Three or more horizontal stripes across the mitred construction, each two rows wide
excerpt: Stripe colours change every two rows across the mitred square, giving horizontal bands that narrow toward the tip as the row count shrinks. Three colours in rotation produce six graduated stripes; the visible diagonal spine interrupts each stripe band for a graphic finish.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 2 (1887). Stripe construction is a standard adaptation of the mitred decrease square.
heroPrompt: A striped mitred crochet square in terracotta, cream, and sage DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Horizontal stripes narrow toward the lower corner, 10 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Each finished square measures 10 × 10 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Mitred square — striped
chartDefinition.caption: Colours rotate every 2 rows. Each row shortens by 2 sts through the central dc2tog.

glossaryTerms.definition: The planned rotation of colours across rows. In a 3-colour 2-row stripe, colours cycle A-A-B-B-C-C-A-A and so on.
Double crochet two together: decreases by one stitch at the midpoint of each row to build the diagonal spine.

give six visible stripes across the 10-row square.

Carry unused colours up the side edge rather than cutting after each stripe. The two-row repeat means each colour rises only a short distance before it is needed again, keeping bulk to a minimum. Fasten off all three ends at the tip and weave in along the edge rows.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 3 g each of three DK-weight cotton colours. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Dc in 2nd ch from hook and in next 8 ch. Dc2tog over next 2 ch. Dc in each remaining 9 ch. Turn. (19 sts.) Ch 1. Dc across to 1 st before centre. Dc2tog over next 2 sts. Dc to end. Turn. (17 sts.)
Join colour B. Work 2 rows as established, decreasing at centre each row. (13 sts after row 4.)
Rows 5–6 (colour C), Rows 7–8 (colour A), Row 9 (colour B), Row 10 (colour C)
Continue in stripe sequence, 2 rows per colour. Row 10 ends with dc2tog over final 2 sts. Fasten off. (1 st.)
Once the striped mitred square is reliable, try the log cabin square — a related rows-based construction that builds outward in strips rather than decreasing inward.
